flo_001: You can recognise it by its dark, dense crown throwing deep shade, on a trunk nearly 4 metres round. It stands in the Giardino dei Semplici on Via Pier Antonio Micheli.
flo_002: You can recognise it by its thick, spongy, deeply fissured cork bark and a sprawling crown spreading over 400 square metres. It stands a short walk from the Micheli Yew in the same garden.
flo_003: You can recognise it by its huge trunk, about 7 metres round, and an asymmetric crown reshaped by a 2014 lightning strike. It stands in the Giardino dei Semplici, often walked past unnoticed.
flo_004: You can recognise it by its height, 29 metres, the tallest tree in the park, with a trunk close to 4.5 metres round. It stands at the western edge of the Parco delle Cascine.
flo_008: You can recognise it by growing beside the winged Pegasus statue on the walled terrace at the top of the garden. It stands in the Giardino del Cavaliere, Boboli Gardens.
flo_009: You can recognise it by its fan-shaped leaves, turning uniform gold and dropping within days each November, on a trunk about 3 metres round. It stands at the edge of Piazzale Michelangelo.
flo_010: You can recognise it by standing in an isolated spot ringed by centuries-old cypresses, now shading children's play equipment. It stands in the Parco di Villa Vogel, Isolotto-Legnaia.
flo_011: You can recognise it by its fluted, silver, heavily buttressed trunk, nearly 6 metres round, carrying a crown far smaller than the trunk suggests. It stands in the Giardino dei Semplici.
flo_012: You can recognise it by its bark flaking into small rounded plates with orange patches underneath, its short trunk fanning into near-equal limbs. It stands in the Giardino dei Semplici.
flo_013: You can recognise it by its lopsided, flag-shaped crown, almost all its weight on one side of a long bare trunk 33.5 metres up. It stands against the wall of the Giardino dei Semplici.
flo_014: You can recognise it by its nodding leading shoot and branch tips hanging in soft grey-green curtains, unlike the stiffer cedars nearby. It stands in the Giardino dei Semplici, 4.2 metres round.
flo_023: You can recognise it by standing apart from the famous double row of cypresses on the Viottolone, its own separate listed specimen. It stands nearer the Pitti Palace end of the Boboli Gardens.
